task_text: What is the average GDP per capita in 2020 for countries that experienced earthquakes in the last 30 days?

arguments.geodataset: Earthquakes occurences and magnitude March 15- February 14 2025

final_response:
## Answer

**Countries that experienced at least one earthquake in the last 30 days: 45**

(The earthquake catalog covers exactly the last 30 days — Jan 16 → Feb 15, 2025 — so all 9,176 events fall in the window. A spatial join of those epicenters onto country boundaries selected the countries below.)

**The 45 countries:**
Indonesia, Chile, Bolivia, Peru, Argentina, India, China, Ethiopia, Tanzania, Morocco, Nicaragua, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Russian Federation, Kyrgyz Republic, Tunisia, Romania, Poland, Greece, Iraq, Italy, Iran (Islamic Rep.), Croatia, Dominican Republic, El Salvador, Guatemala, Myanmar, Afghanistan, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Uganda, Ecuador, Colombia, Portugal, United States, Canada, Mexico, Papua New Guinea, Australia, Fiji, Philippines, Japan, Puerto Rico, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, New Zealand.

**Average GDP per capita (2020, current US$) across those 45 countries:**

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| **Mean** | **US$ 11,865.51** |
| Valid / Missing | 45 / 0 |
| Range | 512.06 – 64,317.40 |
| Std. dev. | 15,191.63 |

A choropleth map of the 2020 GDP per capita for these 45 countries was also generated.

Notes
- Threshold used: **any cataloged earthquake** (M ≥ catalog minimum). If you meant only *felt/damaging* events, the count and average would change — the dataset has a `mag` column I can re-filter on if you'd like a magnitude threshold.
- One minor data detail: the world-boundaries layer has a duplicated polygon for one of these countries (46 geometries vs. 45 unique names), which doesn't affect the average (computed on the 45 unique country rows).
